2. Respondent No. 1 filed Miscellaneous Case No. 233 of 1978 for pre-emption under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act in the Court of Assistant Judge, Bogra, which was subsequently re-numbered as Miscellaneous Case No. 233 of 1988. The petitioner contested the case and it was fixed for hearing on 6-1-83. The petition filed hajira but was absent when the case was taken up for hearing. The Miscellaneous Case was allowed ex parte by judgment and order dated 6-1-83. At the time of ex parte order it was found that the deposit of consideration money was short by Taka 302,50.00 owing to lawyer's mistake in calculation and respondent No. 1 filed a petition under sections 151 and 152 CPC for depicting the short amount which was allowed by the trial Court by a subsequent order dated 6-1-83 and respondent No. 1 deposited the short amount on the same date. On appeal, Miscellaneous Appeal No. 7 of 1983, the learned Additional District Judge, Bogra allowed the same and remanded the case to the trial Court for fresh trial. Respondent No. 1 preferred Civil Revision No. 313 of 1984 in the High Court Division unsuccessfully and the Rule was discharged on 15-6-87. 

 4. In the High Court Division the only point for consideration was whether the acceptance of short amount by the trial Court was in conformity to and in compliance with section 96(3) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. The High Court Division considered the cases of Akhterunnesa and another vs. Habibullah and others, 31 DLR (AD) 87, and Serina Begum and another vs. Mofizul Islam and others, 42 DLR (AD) 77 and following the last-cited decision held that the deposit of short money after the statutory period given under section 96(3) of the Act may be allowed.
